constraints: Include only open tickets that meet the stated attention criteria; exclude tickets waiting on the customer. Use only ticket number, subject, current owner, priority, and last customer-facing reply date. Do not include customer names, email addresses, or message text. The digest must remain a draft until the team lead approves it. Send at most one reminder if approval is missing at noon. Confirm the local time zone before implementation.
dialogue_text:
User: We get a lot of support tickets, and I’d like a weekly digest of the ones that still need attention.
Assistant: When should the digest be prepared, and where should it go?
User: Every Monday at 9 a.m. local time. Put it in our support team’s shared channel.
Assistant: Which tickets should count as needing attention?
User: Include open tickets that have had no customer-facing reply for at least two days, plus any open ticket marked urgent. Exclude tickets that are waiting on the customer.
Assistant: Should the workflow include every matching ticket, or group or prioritize them?
User: Group them by priority, then by age, oldest first. Include the ticket number, subject, current owner, priority, and last customer-facing reply date.
Assistant: Can the workflow post the digest directly, or should someone review it first?
User: Create a draft for the team lead to review. Do not post it to the channel until the lead approves.
Assistant: What should happen if there are no matching tickets, or if the lead has not reviewed the draft?
User: If there are none, make a short draft saying there are no tickets needing attention. If the lead has not approved it by Monday at noon, send them one reminder and leave the draft unposted.
Assistant: Should ticket content such as customer messages be copied into the digest?
User: No. Use only the listed ticket fields, and do not include customer names, email addresses, or message text.
Assistant: I have the selection rules, grouping, review gate, and privacy limits. Is the time zone for “local time” known?
User: Not yet; we’ll confirm that when we connect the support system.
workflow_steps: 1. On the scheduled run, retrieve open support tickets. 2. Exclude tickets waiting on the customer. Include the remaining open tickets if they are marked urgent or have had no customer-facing reply for at least two days. 3. Group matching tickets by priority and sort each group by age, oldest first. 4. Prepare a digest with each ticket's number, subject, current owner, priority, and last customer-facing reply date; do not include customer names, email addresses, or message text. 5. If there are no matching tickets, prepare a short draft stating that there are no tickets needing attention. 6. Submit the draft to the team lead for review and do not post it to the shared channel unless approved. 7. If approval has not been received by Monday at noon, send one reminder to the team lead and leave the draft unposted.
automation_goal: Prepare a privacy-conscious weekly draft digest that helps the support team identify open tickets needing attention and awaits team lead approval before posting.
expected_result: A Monday digest draft, grouped by priority and ordered oldest first, is available for the team lead to review. It is posted to the support team's shared channel only after approval. If no tickets match, the draft says so; if approval is still missing at noon, the lead receives one reminder and the draft remains unposted.
trigger_condition: Every Monday at 9 a.m. local time. The exact time zone has not yet been specified and must be confirmed when the support system is connected.
final_workflow_plan: After confirming the local time zone and connected systems, run every Monday at 9 a.m. Retrieve open support tickets, exclude those waiting on the customer, and select tickets marked urgent or with no customer-facing reply for at least two days. Group the results by priority and order each group oldest first. Build a draft containing only the ticket number, subject, current owner, priority, and last customer-facing reply date; omit customer names, email addresses, and message text. If no tickets match, draft a brief notice that there are no tickets needing attention. Send the draft to the team lead for review, and post it to the support team's shared channel only after approval. If it remains unapproved by Monday at noon, send one reminder to the team lead and leave the draft unposted.
conversation_summary: The user wants a weekly Monday 9 a.m. digest of open support tickets with no customer-facing reply for at least two days or tickets marked urgent, excluding tickets waiting on the customer. The digest should be grouped by priority and then age, oldest first, and prepared as a draft for the team lead. It must not be posted without approval. If unapproved by noon, send one reminder and leave it unposted. The time zone remains to be confirmed.
unresolved_questions: The time zone for the Monday 9 a.m. schedule is not yet known. The support system and shared-channel integration details also need to be confirmed when the system is connected.

constraints: Do not place orders automatically. Keep the original form submission unchanged. Share request details only with people already authorized in the purchasing process. Do not route incomplete requests for approval. Send only one reminder after three business days without a response; leave the request pending afterward.
dialogue_text:
User: I want to automate the intake of equipment purchase requests.
Assistant: What should start the workflow, and what should happen to each request?
User: A new submission in our purchase request form should start it. I need the request checked for required details, then routed for approval.
Assistant: Which details are required, and how should approval routing work?
User: The requester must provide an item description, quantity, estimated cost, department, and a business reason. If any are missing, send the requester a message asking them to update the submission and do not route it yet. Requests under $1,000 go to the department manager. Requests of $1,000 or more need both the department manager and Finance approval.
Assistant: Should the workflow place an order after approval, or stop at recording the decision?
User: Stop after approval. Create a task for the purchasing team with the approved request details. Do not place orders automatically.
Assistant: What should happen if an approver declines or does not respond?
User: If someone declines, notify the requester and purchasing team with the decision and comments. If there is no response after three business days, remind the approver once. Leave the request pending after that; a person can follow up.
Assistant: Should the workflow include any other restrictions?
User: Only people already authorized in our purchasing process should receive request details. Keep the original submission unchanged.
Assistant: Understood. I’ll draft the workflow with the form submission as the trigger, validation before routing, the two approval paths, and a purchasing task only after approval. Is there anything else?
User: No, that covers the process.
workflow_steps: 1. Read the new submission and check for an item description, quantity, estimated cost, department, and business reason. 2. If any required detail is missing, ask the requester to update the submission and pause the workflow without routing it. 3. If the request is complete and estimated cost is under $1,000, route it to the department manager. If the cost is $1,000 or more, route it to the department manager and Finance for approval. 4. If an approver declines, notify the requester and purchasing team with the decision and comments. 5. If an approval is still pending after three business days, send one reminder to the approver; leave the request pending after that. 6. When all required approvals are granted, create a purchasing team task containing the approved request details.
automation_goal: Validate equipment purchase requests, obtain the required approvals, and create a purchasing team task for approved requests without placing an order.
expected_result: A complete, approved request is recorded in a task for the purchasing team. Incomplete, declined, or still-pending requests follow the specified notification or pause behavior, and no order is placed automatically.
trigger_condition: A new submission in the purchase request form.
final_workflow_plan: On each new purchase request form submission, verify that the item description, quantity, estimated cost, department, and business reason are present. If anything is missing, ask the requester to update the submission and stop before approval routing. Route complete requests under $1,000 to the department manager; route requests of $1,000 or more to both the department manager and Finance. If an approver declines, notify the requester and purchasing team with the decision and comments. For requests still awaiting approval after three business days, send one reminder to the approver and then leave the request pending for human follow-up. Once all required approvals are granted, create a task for the purchasing team with the approved request details. Preserve the original submission, limit access to authorized purchasing-process participants, and never place an order automatically. Confirm the connected systems and task fields before implementation.
conversation_summary: The user wants purchase requests submitted through a form validated and routed for approval. Requests below $1,000 require department manager approval; requests at or above $1,000 also require Finance approval. Missing information blocks routing. Approved requests create a task for purchasing, but the workflow must not place orders. Declines generate notifications, and one reminder is sent after three business days without a response.
unresolved_questions: The user did not specify which form, messaging, approval, or task-management systems should be connected, or the exact fields and destinations for the purchasing task. These implementation details need confirmation before configuration.
